newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Svyazinvest to start telecoms share issues in 98.
newsitem.headline: Svyazinvest to start telecoms share issues in 98.

text.p: Russian telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, in which a Russian and foreign financial consortium bought a quarter stake last week, said on Thursday its subsidiaries would start conducting new share issues in 1998.
"We are now preparing several regional companies for new issues -- a draft government order...has even been prepared," company chief executive Nail Izmailov told a news conference.
"Starting in 1998, based on our capabilities and certain agreements already reached with our new companions, we will turn to mass new issues."

Svyazinvest, which holds major stakes in 89 regional and other telecom companies, including international long distance carrier Rostelekom, has in the past opposed some of its subsidiaries' plans to issue shares.
Svyazinvest did not have the funds to subscribe to new shares, but did not want to see its holdings diluted.
But its new owners pack considerable financial muscle.

The consortium which bought the 25 percent plus one share stake in Svyazinvest for $1.875 billion was led by Russia's third largest bank Uneximbank and includes Morgan Stanley Asset Management, Deutsche Bank's Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and U.S. financier George Soros's Quantum Fund.
Uneximbank head Vladimir Potanin said the consortium would support the share issues.
"We are definitely looking at the possibility of participating in new issues by subsidiaries," Potanin said, saying Svyazinvest would retain its current stakes in any new issue.
"We consider that it will be an important means of attracting investment specifically to regional companies."
